en.html:
—Apparently I had been standing there, motionless, for some time.
I turned toward the voice. My mother was in the doorway, looking at me with worry.

I do not believe I had been vacant for several minutes... though perhaps I had. Reality came back all at once and I could not find my footing.

en.html:
I could find no ground to deny it, so I kept my mouth shut. I did not intend to involve the townspeople. The bandits were a problem for the whole town, true, but the present agreement with the senior house was something I had made for my own private need.

I should not make other people share the danger.
I will admit it: a man like the old gentleman would see through me that easily.

　成程、あの御老人であれば、俺のそんな心理くらい
見通すだろう。

en.html:
Kageaki"There is no alternative."
統"............ Hai Ram. What a troublesome son."
Kageaki"Forgive me."
統"I should have raised you a bit lazier. Cut corners. Take the easy road."
Kageaki"I tried my utmost to follow your example, Subaru ji."
統"...The only part of you that is fully grown is the cheek. Honestly, na."
統"Fine. But I am coming with you."
Kageaki"That is not permitted."
統"'Not permitted', my foot, I am coming. Which mother lets her son walk alone into a place like that?"
Kageaki"Overprotective mothers have recently become a social problem."
統"A mother who sends her son alone into an armed gang of looters is also a social problem. It is called abuse, I think."
Kageaki"Would it not rather be juvenile delinquency on the son's part? ...No. That is not the issue."
Kageaki"The senior head ordered me to settle this by my own ability. I cannot borrow your strength."
統"But he also said you may use people from town. I am a person from town. Checkmate, beta."
Kageaki"..."
統"Heh. Clumsy son. You are ten years too early to beat your mother in an argument—"
Kageaki"The senior head did not say people from town. He said men from town."
Kageaki"Please give it up, Subaru ji."
統"...It has not even been ten seconds... And OYE, BUDDHE! You old idiot! Do you hate me that much!?"
Kageaki"Besides... Subaru ji. I cannot leave Hikaru alone."
統"..."
Kageaki"While I am away, please protect Hikaru. I ask this of you."
統"............ Aaah!"
統"Uff!"
統"Damn it! Zara bhi cute nahin hai tu!!"

In any case, work would not come back until the stock the bandits had carried off was replaced. Even if I went in, there was nothing for me to do.

Besides, settling the bandit problem would benefit the company too. When I explained the situation and asked for leave, the president approved it at once without a murmur, and even made it paid.

...Though it seemed less an expression of hope than an advance payment of condolence money. The look on his face, hope and resignation wrestling, stood, by my reading, at one to nine, with resignation well ahead.

One could hardly blame him.

en.html:
I straightened my posture and took up a listening stance. Anything my foster mother introduced with such a preface had to be worth the effort.

She too had learned the Yoshino style from her own father, as her daughter had. When Hikaru asked to train, the senior house disliked it but in the end let it pass in silence, for the plainest of reasons: there was already a precedent in my foster mother.

Her skill, moreover, is far beyond the ordinary. She never makes a point of displaying it, but what one glimpses in her everyday carriage matches even that of Hikaru, the genius.

Advice from such a person could be treated neither idly nor lightly. As I waited in a posture of respectful hearing, my foster mother told me:

en.html:
My foster mother was right.
I was ashamed of how shallow my thinking had been.

Kill even one, and a grudge is born that cannot be washed away. Once that happens, nothing waits beyond but a swamp of mutual destruction.

Even if I had started this alone, the town could not stay out of it. Great numbers would die, bandits and townspeople alike.

That was the very worst ending, the one I most wanted to avoid at any cost, and I had been walking straight toward it. Not a solution at all: the whole purpose turned upside down.
